spatial_claims.claim: After superposition, A is placed on C and AB along CD, so B coincides with D (since AB = CD)
After AB coincides with CD, segment AEB either coincides with CFD, or falls inside, outside, or intersects it
If segments do not coincide, then on the same straight line CD, on the same side, there exist two similar but unequal segments of circles

configuration_map: Two equal straight lines AB and CD with similar circle segments AEB and CFD. After superposition (A placed on C, AB along CD), B coincides with D. The segment AEB is placed on the same side of CD as CFD. If non-coincident, two similar unequal segments exist on the same line on the same side, contradicting 3.23.
pass_reason: The proof makes minimal spatial claims (superposition placement, same-side positioning) that are all mutually consistent. The superposition method validly places AEB on the same side as CFD, and non-coincidence correctly yields the configuration forbidden by Proposition 3.23. No angle decompositions, no interior/exterior point claims, and no ray betweenness issues arise.
